title: Not every Apostle need write — a few inspired books serve the whole Church
source_text: XV. Denique non est majoris ponderis & momenti quod urget Bellarminus, nempe, si Deo fuisset propositum Evangelii doctrinam per Apostolos literis consignare, futurum fuisse ut, vel singuli Apostoli corpus Evangelicae doctrinae conscriberent in usum provinciarum illarum quibus praedicabant, vel certe omnes simul congregati, antequam discederent in suas provincias, librum aliquem communem ederent: Etenim ut istud Dei propositum ratum fieret, & mandaretur executioni, suffecit ut nonnulli ex Apostolis & Evangelistis scribendi curam Deo inspirante susciperent. Nam scripta a paucis edita potuerunt universae Ecclesiae usui esse, & inservire fidelibus omnium provinciarum. Neque opus fuit hac de re Apostolos in communi consulere, cum Deus non minus singulos seorsim inspiraret, quam omnes simul congregatos. Adde quod scripta divina non ex hominum consilio, sed ex Dei immediato & extraordinario afflatu fieri debuerunt.
pass_a_gloss: Finally, what Bellarmine urges is of no greater weight or moment — namely, that if God had proposed to consign the doctrine of the Gospel to letters through the Apostles, either each Apostle would have written a body of Evangelical doctrine for the use of those provinces in which they preached, or certainly all gathered together before departing to their provinces would have issued some common book: For for that purpose of God to stand and be put into execution, it was enough that some of the Apostles and Evangelists, God inspiring, should take up the care of writing. For writings published by a few could be of use to the universal Church and serve the faithful of all provinces. Nor was it needful that the Apostles consult in common on this, since God inspires individuals separately no less than all gathered together. Add that divine writings ought to come not from men's counsel, but from God's immediate and extraordinary breath.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine: if God meant a written Gospel, every Apostle — or a joint council — would have issued a full body of doctrine.
Reply: a few inspired writers suffice for the whole Church's use.
No need for an Apostles' committee — God inspires persons as well as assemblies.
Sacred books arise from God's immediate breath, not from human planning.

lemmas.gloss: each Apostle a full Gospel body

rejected: every Apostle must publish a provincial corpus
